description: Magnesium is a chemical element with symbol Mg and atomic number 12. It is a shiny gray metal having a low density, low melting point, and high chemical reactivity. Like the other alkaline earth metals, it occurs naturally only in combination with other elements and almost always has an oxidation state of +2.
uses: Magnesium is used primarily as a component in strong and lightweight alloys that contain aluminium. It is essential to all cells and some 300 enzymes in the human body, and magnesium compounds are used medicinally as common laxatives and antacids such as milk of magnesia, and to stabilize abnormal nerve excitation or blood vessel spasm. Magnesium is also widely used as a reducing agent and may be used as an igniter for thermite.
characteristics: Magnesium is a gray-white lightweight metal, two-thirds the density of aluminium, with the lowest melting point (650 °C) and lowest boiling point (1,090 °C) of all the alkaline earth metals. Pure polycrystalline magnesium is brittle and easily fractures along shear bands but becomes much more malleable when alloyed with small amounts of other metals. It reacts readily with air to form a thin passivation coating of magnesium oxide that inhibits further corrosion, and the free metal burns with a brilliant-white light.
